quests.title: Commission: The Winter Stores
quests.description: The board is asking for money as well as work now. Four cold-bench tonics and 900 coins lays in a winter's stock the valley has never once had, held at the waystation and the infirmary both.

completion_milestones.title: Stores, Not Rations
completion_milestones.text: The valley has a winter's stock laid in for the first time in living memory, funded out of the tower's own takings. Tarn pointed out that it is the first year anybody has had to decide where to put things rather than what to do without.

quests.title: Commission: The Reading Room
quests.description: Six archive lights and 1,400 coins turns Ione's corner into a room other people can work in. She has not asked. Brin has, on her behalf, twice.

completion_milestones.title: A Room Other People Can Work In
completion_milestones.text: The archive corner is a reading room. Ione has stopped apologising for the light and started complaining about the noise, which everybody agrees is an improvement. The eleven months sit in the open on the middle table, and people come up to read them.

quests.title: Commission: The Standing Survey
quests.description: Eight resonance draughts and 2,600 coins puts a permanent measure on the valley: bloom counts, well readings and yields, taken every season by people who are paid to take them. Nobody has to notice a collapse by accident again.

completion_milestones.title: Nobody Notices By Accident Again
completion_milestones.text: The valley measures itself now, every season, by people paid to do it. It took a keeper counting eleven where the log said ninety to work out what was happening, and the whole point of the survey is that the next person will not have to be that observant to find out in time.

quests.title: Commission: The Relief Post
quests.description: Five carry-down cordials and 1,800 coins puts a stocked post at the head of the switchback: a stretcher, a lamp kept filled, and something that holds a person still for the four hours it takes four people to carry them down. Wren costed this eleven years ago and was told the valley could not afford it.

completion_milestones.title: Four Hours, With Something In It
completion_milestones.text: There is a post at the head of the switchback now, with a lamp somebody fills and a shelf somebody restocks. The four hours down are the same four hours. What has changed is that they are no longer the whole of the treatment, and Wren has stopped writing the phrase 'arrived too late' in a hand that gets smaller each time.

quests.title: Commission: The Standing Road
quests.description: Six long-haul draughts and 3,400 coins puts a scheduled run on the road: two carts a week, both directions, in weather, whether or not there is a full load to justify it. Tarn has argued for eleven years that a valley a road merely passes is not on the road at all.

completion_milestones.title: Both Directions, In Weather
completion_milestones.text: Two carts a week, posted on a board in the square where anybody can read the days. Half of them leave under-loaded and go anyway, which is the entire point and the part that cost 3,400 coins. Tarn says a road forgets a place that only sends for things, and remembers one that sends things out.

quests.title: Commission: The Second Bench
quests.description: Six purified draughts and 5,200 coins fits out a second bench in the entry laboratory and pays somebody to stand at it for a year: a stipend, a reference shelf they can measure their own work against, and a formula book that is allowed to be wrong in the margins. The draughts are the reference shelf. It is the plainest thing in the book, which is the point — the first thing you ever learned, made well enough that somebody else can learn it from the bottle.

completion_milestones.title: Somebody Else's Turn At It
completion_milestones.text: A second bench along the east wall of the entry laboratory, a stipend for a year, and six purified draughts on a shelf above it to measure against. The tower has been one person's for twenty years twice over, and both times that was the problem rather than the arrangement. It is not the arrangement now. Whoever stands at that bench will be wrong about things, in the margins, in ink, where somebody can read it.

quests.title: Commission: The Teaching Place
quests.description: Eight Masterwork second-draft tonics and 6,800 coins turn the second bench's one-year stipend into a standing teaching place: wages, lodging, paper, and a line in the town budget that comes back next year whoever happens to sit there. The bottles are the first reference shelf made entirely from somebody's corrected work.

completion_milestones.title: The Line That Comes Back Next Year
completion_milestones.text: The second bench is funded again before its first year has run out. Wages, lodging and paper are a standing line now, not a rescue and not a favour. The name beside it can change. The line does not. A tower that can teach its work is no longer one person's tower.
